first.rationale: Competitor entry pricing is directly attacking the SMB segment where we have proven wins. Memory 73 shows promotional pricing lifted acquisition and time-to-first-value in price-sensitive SMB accounts without measurable retention harm. Memory 31 demonstrates signup simplification also drove SMB activation. We're seeing activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding down 4% QoQ—both metrics improved by prior promotional and simplification interventions. Verification of memory 73 (the most directly relevant competitive response) and memory 31 (supporting the SMB playbook) will confirm the mechanics before scaling. A standard experiment on targeted promotional pricing addresses the immediate competitive threat in our most vulnerable segment while defending long-term revenue quality—SMBs acquired via pricing remain qualified if they reach first meaningful action (supported by memory 86 showing onboarding improvements stick). Enterprise sales assist is premature without addressing core activation decline; referral incentives work best with healthy baseline activation; activation messaging alone won't overcome price resistance in current competitive context.
